_meta.note: Every rule is backed by a source URL that was opened (WebFetch) during research. Dates in brackets are the source page's own date or version where shown. Not legal advice; local rules can be stricter.

sup.t: On lakes, carry a life jacket or 50 N buoyancy aid once you are more than 300 m from shore; on rivers, carry one at all times.
src: vks Merkblatt Nr. 6 Stehpaddler (in force 1 May 2022)

sup.t: Every person on board needs a buoyancy aid of at least 50 N; beyond 300 m from shore on a lake it must be a suitable vest.
SUPs are not registered, but the owner's name and address must be clearly visible on the board.
At night or in poor visibility, show a clearly visible white all-round light.
SUPs may only be moved by paddle; motors and motor assistance are not allowed.
src: vks Merkblatt Nr. 6 Stehpaddler (2022), Art. 121 Abs. 5 BSV

sup.t: Example: Strandbad Auslikon (Wetzikon) asks for an ID card as deposit for SUP rental; under-16s need a parent present to sign.
On border lakes (Constance, Geneva, Lugano, Maggiore), carry ID: crossing the lake can mean entering another country.

kayak.t: No licence or registration for private canoes/kayaks, but the owner's name and address must be visible on the boat.
src: Swiss Canoe – Rechtliches im Paddelsport (28 Jul 2022)

kayak.t: On rivers, and on lakes beyond the shore zones, carry a buoyancy aid (SN EN ISO 12402-5) that fits each paddler.
src: Swiss Canoe – Rechtliches im Paddelsport (2022), Art. 134/134a BSV

kayak.t: The outer shore zone on Swiss lakes ends 300 m from the shore.
Show a white all-round light at night or in poor visibility.
src: Swiss Canoe – Rechtliches im Paddelsport (2022), Art. 25 BSV

kayak.t: Paddle boats must give way to motorboats; keep about 25 m away from reeds and water-lily beds.
src: Swiss Canoe – Rechtliches im Paddelsport (2022), Art. 44 and 53 BSV

kayak.t: Commercial white-water trips from grade III need a cantonal permit and a certified operator.
src: Kanton Appenzell AR – Merkblatt Risikoaktivitäten (1 Jan 2019)

kayak.t: On Lake Constance, canoes and kayaks must carry a buoyancy aid outside the 300 m shore zone.

row.t: Rowing boats need no licence and have no minimum age.
Rowing boats on lakes need not carry rescue devices inside the shore zones (up to 300 m).
src: Swiss Canoe – Rechtliches im Paddelsport (2022), Art. 134 Abs. 5 BSV

pedal.t: Example: Pedalo Luzern rents pedal boats from age 14, with a CHF 20 deposit, only in good weather.

boatrent.t: Motorboats of 6 kW or less can be driven without a licence; the minimum age is 14.
Example: Pedalo Luzern lets you drive its small motorboats (up to 8 people) without a licence.
Example: s'Lüchttürmli boat rental (Lake Lucerne) needs no licence; you get a short introduction first.
Example: Strandbad Auslikon takes an ID card as rental deposit.
On border lakes (Constance, Geneva, Lugano, Maggiore), carry ID in case of police or customs checks.

motorboat.t: Motorboats over 6 kW (8 PS) need a Category A licence; minimum age 18.
Motorboats of 6 kW or less need no licence; minimum age 14.
There is no learner's licence; practice drives need a licence holder of the same category on board.
Category A and D licence holders need a medical check every two years from age 75.
Maximum 10 km/h inside the shore zones (up to 300 m from shore).
src: Kanton Luzern – Erläuterungen Vernehmlassung (24 Sep 2015), Art. 53 BSV

sail.t: Sailing boats with more than 15 m² sail area need a Category D licence; minimum age 14.
Sailing boats with 15 m² sail area or less need no licence and have no minimum age.
A sailing boat with an engine over 6 kW also needs a Category A licence (can be limited to sailing boats); minimum age 18.
On Lake Constance, sailing dinghies and multihulls must carry a buoyancy aid.

windsurf.t: Windsurfers and kitesurfers must give way to all other vessels.
On Lake Constance, sailboards must carry a buoyancy aid and show the owner's name and address.

kite.t: Kitesurfing is allowed on Swiss waters since 15 Feb 2016, unless a canton restricts or bans it locally.
Kite only by day (08:00–21:00) and in clear visibility.
src: Weblaw Wassersportkommentar – Kitesurfen, Art. 54 Abs. 1 BSV

kite.t: Liability insurance is mandatory for kiteboards (minimum cover CHF 750,000); many private policies exclude kiting.
src: Weblaw Wassersportkommentar – Kitesurfen, Art. 153 Abs. 2bis and 155 BSV

kite.t: The board must show the owner's name and address; a phone number is recommended.
Inside the shore zones, cantons can restrict kiting to marked launch lanes.
src: Kanton Luzern – Erläuterungen Vernehmlassung (2015), Art. 54 Abs. 2ter BSV

kite.t: Kiters must give way to everyone; in canton Bern keep 200 m from passenger ships and their piers.
Zurich: allowed on Lake Zurich (not the city basin, not within 150 m of piers, bathing areas or harbour mouths); banned on Greifensee, Pfäffikersee and Türlersee.
On Lake Constance, kiteboards must carry a buoyancy aid.

wing.t: Swiss law does not yet clearly cover wingfoiling; the kiteboard definition doesn't mention it, so check local rules first.

surf.t: River waves such as Thun need strong skills: getting from the bank into the wave in cold water takes experience.
src: Newly Swissed – River surfing in Switzerland (2 May 2021, updated 7 Mar 2025)

surf.t: The Bremgarten wave (Reuss) works at water levels of about 1.8–2.6 m, mostly May to September.
src: Newly Swissed – River surfing in Switzerland (2021/2025)

dive.t: Lake Zurich: diving is allowed except in shipping lanes, narrow channels, harbour entrances, near official moorings and within 100 m of passenger-ship piers.
Most Swiss lakes count as altitude dives (from about 300 m above sea level); adjust your dive computer and plan, e.g. with an Altitude Diver course.
src: PADI Blog – Altitude Diver in Swiss lakes

dive.t: Lake Constance: show the blue-and-white flag 'A' when diving from shore, and on the boat or a buoy when diving from the water.

raft.t: Commercial rafting from white-water grade III needs a cantonal permit; only certified companies get one.
src: Kanton Appenzell AR – Merkblatt Risikoaktivitäten (1 Jan 2019), RiskG/RiskV

raft.t: Example (Interlaken): minimum age 8 for family rafting, 10 on the Simme, 14 on the Lütschine; max 125 kg; swimming recommended but not always required.

canyon.t: Commercial canyoning needs a cantonal permit; only certified companies get one.
src: Kanton Appenzell AR – Merkblatt Risikoaktivitäten (1 Jan 2019), RiskG/RiskV

canyon.t: Example (Outdoor Interlaken): minimum age 12, max weight 125 kg; no swim test, but you should be comfortable in water.

wake.t: Lake Zurich: water-skiing only by day and in clear visibility, between 08:00 and 21:00; not allowed on other lakes in canton Zurich.
The towing boat's driver needs a Category A licence if the engine is over 6 kW.
Lake Constance: a second person must watch the skier, max two skiers at once, keep 50 m from others, and stay out of the shore zone.

fishing.t: Graubünden: you need a fishing knowledge certificate (SaNa) to buy an annual or monthly fishing permit.

motorboat.t: Motorboats over 15 PS (11.03 kW) need an official Sportbootführerschein (See or Binnen).
Minimum age for the sea licence (SBF See) is 16.
Exceptions: the Rhine needs a Rheinpatent, Lake Constance a Bodensee licence, and some Berlin waters need SBF Binnen for all craft.

boatrent.t: Boats up to 15 PS can be driven without a licence.

wake.t: Lake Constance (DE/AT/CH): an observer must be on board, max two skiers, 50 m from others, not in the shore zone.

motorboat.t: A boat licence (Patent) is generally required for motorboats; recreational boats under 4.4 kW are exempt.
Foreign licences and Lake Constance licences are accepted for recreational boating (not on official waterways for the latter).

boatrent.t: Boats under 4.4 kW can be driven without a licence.

motorboat.t: A licence is needed for engines over 30 kW (about 40 hp), or for any boat more than 6 nautical miles offshore.
src: ICOMIA – Italy, boat licensing (rule from July 2005)

motorboat.t: Minimum licence age: 16 for boats up to 10 m, 18 for boats over 10 m.
Jet skis (PWC) always need a licence.

sail.t: Minimum age 14 to skipper a sailing boat with more than 4 m² of sail.

motorboat.t: A permis plaisance is required when the engine is over 4.5 kW (6 hp).
The licence comes as 'côtière' (sea) or 'eaux intérieures' (rivers/lakes), with an offshore 'hauturière' extension.

boatrent.t: Boats with engines up to 6 hp can be rented without a licence.
src: Click&Boat Help – licence to rent a boat (12 Apr 2023)

boatrent.t: No licence needed for motorboats up to 5 m and 11.26 kW (15 hp), within 2 nautical miles of the coast; minimum age 18.
The same licence-free rule covers sailing boats up to 6 m.

motorboat.t: Bigger boats and jet skis need a nautical licence; foreign licences on rented boats need Harbour Master (Capitanía) authorisation, usually arranged by the rental firm.
Croatia requires a boating licence even for small motorboats; as of Feb 2023 there was no licence-free rental category.
A proposed exemption (rental boats ≤5 m, ≤5 kW, within 500 m of shore, age 18+) was not yet in force when reported.

boatrent.t: Rental platforms report small motorboats up to 30 hp can be driven without a licence (some say 15 hp for outboards); minimum age 18.
src: Borrow A Boat – Greece licence (updated 18 May 2026)

charter.t: Bareboat sailing charters need a recognised licence such as the ICC; many bases also want a second experienced crew member.

motorboat.t: The entry 'Principiante' licence (from age 8) covers boats up to 5 m and 4.5 kW, by day, within 1 nautical mile.
src: Click&Boat Blog PT – cartas de marinheiro (Jan 2023)

motorboat.t: Jet skis need a 'Marinheiro' licence (age 16+): daytime only, within 1 nm and more than 300 m from beaches.
src: Click&Boat Blog PT – cartas de marinheiro (2023)

motorboat.t: You need a vaarbewijs if the boat can go faster than 20 km/h or is longer than 15 m; it can be used from age 18.

boatrent.t: Boats up to 15 m that cannot exceed 20 km/h need no licence.

motorboat.t: No licence or test is needed to drive a private boat in the UK.
src: Aquavista – Do you need a licence for boating

motorboat.t: On inland waterways the boat itself needs a licence/registration from the navigation authority (e.g. Canal & River Trust, Environment Agency, Broads Authority).
src: Aquavista – Do you need a licence for boating

motorboat.t: 36 states require some boater education; rules and minimum ages vary by state.
States accept each other's NASBLA-approved boater education cards; carry it on board.

sup.t: Outside swimming/surfing areas a paddleboard is a vessel: carry a life jacket per person, a whistle, and a light after sunset.
Wear a buoyancy aid sized so you can climb back onto the board.
On rivers and flowing tidal water, use a quick-release waist leash, not an ankle leash.
Avoid offshore wind; check forecast and tides, carry a phone on your body, and tell someone your plan.

kayak.t: Wear a buoyancy aid, carry a way to call for help, check the weather, tell someone your plans, and paddle within your ability.

dive.t: To dive without a professional you need an Open Water certification (e.g. PADI/SSI); it allows dives to 18 m.
Try dives (Discover Scuba) start at age 10, go to 12 m max, and are always with an instructor.
Junior Open Water from age 10; ages 10–11 max 12 m with a pro or certified parent.
The 'Scuba Diver' level only allows dives to 12 m under a professional's direct supervision.
Fill in the Diver Medical Questionnaire (UHMS/DAN, June 2020); some 'yes' answers need a doctor's sign-off before diving.
src: PADI Pros Blog – New medical screening (14 Jul 2020)

dive.t: Don't dive alone without proper training; solo diving is illegal in some areas and banned by many operators.

freedive.t: PADI Freediver course: minimum age 15 (Basic Freediver 12).
You must swim 200 m non-stop (or 300 m with mask, fins and snorkel) and complete a medical form.

charter.t: European charter companies usually ask for an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or equal licence.
